title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2
hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)  Multi-user Droplet Combustion Appartatus (MDCA)

sources.title: Cool-flame Extinction During N-Alkane Droplet Combustion in Microgravity
A Burke-Schumann Analysis of Dual-Flame Structure Supported by a Burning Droplet

variables_studied: Droplet spacing and initial size in a binary linear array
key_findings: The experiments aim to study the role of liquid-phase mixing on the burning characteristics of bi-component fuel droplets.
The primary goal is to provide benchmark experimental data on bi-component droplet combustion over a wide range of initial conditions.

conditions.label: Decane droplet combustion
evidence: The chamber was filled with the appropriate atmosphere, which was varied in pressure between 0.5 atm to 3.0 atm and O2 concentration between 0.1 to 0.4 mole fraction

conditions.label: n-decane, 21% O2, 0.5 atm pressure
evidence: 21% oxygen and 79% nitrogen mixture at 0.5 atm pressure

conditions.label: n-decane, 25% O2, 0.5 atm pressure
evidence: Figure 1b (R374) shows the combustion characteristics for a 3.79 mm n-decane droplet burning at a slightly increased oxygen concentration of 25% and the rest being nitrogen at 0.5 atm pressure.

paper_findings.text: Large n-alkane droplets exhibited quasi-steady low-temperature burning and extinction following radiative extinction of the visible flame while smaller droplets burned to completion or disruptively extinguished.
The visible flame diameter initially increases with time and then it decreases until the droplet micro-explodes 26 seconds after ignition.
With the reduced oxygen concentration the overall radiative heat loss decreases due to reduced flame temperature.
Cool-flame temperatures are greater than that of the hot-flame.
A dominant cool-flame is established with fuel leakage of only 50% and relative heat of combustion of only 10%.
With the heat of combustion of the cool-flame around 20% of the hot-flame, a weak cool-flame is established when the fuel leakage is high.
